Do: Use scroll-behavior smooth so anchor links glide to the target section
Don't: Jump instantly to the anchor with no transition
Code Bad: <a href='#section'> with no smooth-scroll CSS

Do: Add scroll-margin-top equal to the nav height on anchor targets so headings land below the fixed nav
Don't: Let the fixed nav cover the section heading after an anchor jump
Code Good: scroll-mt-20 on the target section (nav is h-20)
Code Bad: Anchor target hidden under the sticky navbar

Do: Visually indicate the current page or section in the nav (color + underline or weight)
Don't: Leave every nav link identical so users lose their place
Code Good: aria-current='page' + text-primary on the active item
Code Bad: All nav links styled the same

Do: Preserve browser history so back returns to the previous view (list scroll position and filters included)
Don't: Break the back button with location.replace or state that vanishes on back
Code Bad: location.replace() for normal navigation

Do: Reflect filter/search/tab state in the URL so results can be shared and restored
Don't: Keep dynamic state only in memory behind a single static URL
Code Bad: One URL for every filter combination

Do: Animate at most 1-2 key elements per view so motion directs attention
Don't: Animate everything that can move (cards + icons + badges at once)
Code Bad: animate-bounce on 5+ elements in one view

Do: Bind primary interactions to click/tap because hover does not exist on touch devices
Don't: Reveal critical actions or info on hover only
Code Bad: onMouseEnter as the only path to an action

Do: Reserve infinite/looping animation for loading indicators only
Don't: Loop decorative animation on static UI (icons badges arrows)
Code Good: animate-spin on a spinner while loading
Code Bad: animate-bounce looping on a decorative icon

Do: Define a fixed z-index scale (10/20/30/50) and assign layers by role
Don't: Escalate with arbitrary huge values until it renders on top
Code Good: z-10 dropdown / z-20 sticky nav / z-50 modal
Code Bad: z-[9999] to win a stacking fight

Do: Verify content fits before applying overflow-hidden; use overflow-auto when content can grow
Don't: Blindly apply overflow-hidden and clip focus rings badges or Thai ascenders
Code Bad: overflow-hidden truncating visible content

Do: Account for safe areas and other fixed elements (sticky nav + bottom booking bar) when positioning fixed UI
Don't: Stack multiple fixed elements that overlap each other or the iOS home indicator
Code Bad: Two fixed bars overlapping at the bottom edge

Do: Know that transform/filter/opacity create a new stacking context that traps children's z-index
Don't: Expect a child z-index to escape its parent's stacking context
Code Good: Raise z-index on the parent that owns the context
Code Bad: z-[9999] on a child inside a transformed parent

Do: Use dvh (dynamic viewport height) for full-height mobile layouts because browser chrome shrinks 100vh
Don't: Use 100vh full-screen layouts that overflow when the mobile URL bar shows
Code Bad: h-screen (100vh) on a mobile full-page layout

Do: Keep at least 8px gap between adjacent touch targets to prevent mis-taps
Don't: Pack tappable elements edge-to-edge (calendar days filter chips icon rows)
Code Bad: gap-0 between 44px targets

Do: Keep vertical scroll as the primary gesture; avoid horizontal swipe as the only way to reach content
Don't: Override system gestures (edge-swipe back) or trap content in swipe-only carousels
Code Good: Horizontal card row with visible scrollbar + partial next card
Code Bad: Swipe-only carousel with no scroll affordance

Do: Apply touch-action manipulation on interactive elements to remove the double-tap-zoom delay
Don't: Leave the mobile default so taps feel laggy on controls
Code Bad: No touch optimization on tap-heavy UI

Do: Contain overscroll where accidental pull-to-refresh loses state (modals maps full-screen sheets)
Don't: Leave default overscroll so a scroll flick reloads and discards form state
Code Bad: Default overscroll on a full-screen overlay

Do: Use the semantic input type (email tel url number date) for validation hints and the right mobile keyboard
Don't: Use type='text' for everything
Code Good: type='tel' for phone / type='email' for email
Code Bad: type='text' for a phone field

Do: Set the correct autocomplete tokens so browsers fill name/phone/email correctly
Don't: Set autocomplete='off' everywhere or omit tokens on identity fields
Code Bad: autocomplete='off' on the inquiry form

Do: Mark required fields explicitly (asterisk or required text) before the user submits
Don't: Make users guess which fields are required and learn from errors
Code Bad: No indication until submit fails

Do: Provide a show/hide toggle so users can verify the password while typing
Don't: Force blind typing with no visibility toggle
Code Good: Eye toggle button with aria-label='แสดงรหัสผ่าน'
Code Bad: Password field with no reveal option

Do: Set inputmode so mobile shows the matching keyboard (numeric for OTP/price decimal for coordinates)
Don't: Show the full text keyboard for number-only fields
Code Bad: Default keyboard for a 6-digit OTP

Do: Keep input font-size at 16px or larger so iOS Safari does not auto-zoom on focus
Don't: Use small text (14px or less) on mobile inputs causing viewport zoom-jump
Code Bad: text-sm (14px) on a mobile input

Do: Write mobile styles as the default and enhance upward with md:/lg: breakpoints
Don't: Design desktop-first and patch mobile with max-width overrides
Code Good: Default mobile + md: lg: xl: additive classes
Code Bad: Desktop default + max-width media queries

Do: Test at the common widths 320 375 414 768 1024 1440 before calling responsive work done
Don't: Verify only on your own device/window size
Code Bad: Single-width development

Do: Ensure page content never exceeds viewport width; only intentional rows scroll horizontally within their own container
Don't: Ship a page-level horizontal scrollbar on mobile from one overflowing element
Code Good: max-w-full + overflow-x-auto on the wide element only
Code Bad: Fixed-width child pushing the page wider than the viewport

Do: Wrap wide tables in their own horizontal scroll container or reflow to cards on mobile
Don't: Let a dashboard table break or squash the page layout on small screens
Code Good: overflow-x-auto wrapper around the bookings table
Code Bad: Table wider than the viewport distorting the page

Do: Use locale-aware or relative dates (th-TH Buddhist-era awareness) so dates read unambiguously
Don't: Show ambiguous numeric formats like 01/02/03
Code Good: Intl.DateTimeFormat('th-TH' { dateStyle: 'medium' }) or 2 ชั่วโมงที่แล้ว
Code Bad: Raw 01/02/03 strings

Do: Format large numbers with thousand separators or abbreviations (pair with tabular-nums per DESIGN.md)
Don't: Render long unformatted numbers users must parse digit by digit
Code Bad: 1234567 raw in the price/stat UI

Do: Debounce input and show suggestions as the user types (recent searches + popular provinces)
Don't: Require a full query and an enter press before any feedback
Code Bad: No suggestions on the search field

Do: Show position in multi-step flows with a step indicator (host onboarding booking steps)
Don't: Hide how many steps remain in a wizard
Code Good: ขั้นตอนที่ 2 จาก 4 indicator
Code Bad: Multi-step form with no progress cue

Do: Provide a skip-to-main-content link as the first focusable element on nav-heavy pages
Don't: Force keyboard users to tab through the whole navbar on every page
Code Good: ข้ามไปยังเนื้อหา
Code Bad: Dozens of tab stops before the content

Do: Label AI-generated content and assistants clearly so users know they are not talking to a human
Don't: Present AI output or an AI chat as if it came from a person
Code Good: ผู้ช่วย AI label on the assistant surface
Code Bad: Fake human persona with no AI label

Do: Stream assistant responses token by token so users see progress immediately
Don't: Hold a spinner until the full response is ready (10s+ dead wait)
Code Bad: Spinner until 100% complete

Do: Offer thumbs up/down or regenerate on AI answers to collect quality signals
Don't: Ship read-only AI output with no way to flag a bad answer
Code Good: Feedback buttons under each AI response
Code Bad: Static output only
